subject: Clarifying tail-latency needs and pilot path for ModularRetail
messages:
From: Alex Guerrero <alex@modularretail.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 13:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: demo + traffic profile + latency question

Jordan —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. ModularRetail is excited by the latency numbers you showed. A couple quick clarifications so we can decide whether Hosted is viable or we need a Dedicated pool:

- Typical model: 13B autoregressive, ~64 token responses, prompt + response ~= 120 tokens
- Steady-state QPS: 120 requests/sec daytime, spikes to ~220 QPS for 30–90s during peak minutes
- Target tail SLA: p95 <= 50ms, p99 <= 120ms (we care most about p95)
- Concurrency expectation: up to 8 concurrent streams per user during peak campaigns

I've attached a sample_load_scenarios.csv with per-endpoint breakdown and a short note on our preferred rollout window (holiday catalog launches).

Questions: based on that profile, can Hosted API meet p95 <= 50ms reliably, or would you recommend Dedicated? We also care about cold-start variability for autoscaling and whether prefix/KV caching helps our pattern (lots of similar prompts).

Also copying procurement if we move toward reserved capacity — need to understand commitment sizing and contract lead time.

Appreciate a short recommendation and next steps.

—Alex
Alex Guerrero
Sr Product Manager, ModularRetail

Attachments: sample-load-scenarios.csv (text/csv)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alex Guerrero <alex@modularretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Oct 2027 13:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: demo + traffic profile + latency question

Alex — great context, thanks for the details and for the CSV. Very helpful. Short answers up-front then a recommended path:

1) Can Hosted meet p95 <= 50ms?
   - For your steady-state (120 QPS) and typical sequence length, Hosted can approach that p95 in optimistic conditions (warm, cached, moderate concurrency).
   - However, given your spike to ~220 QPS and the strict p95 target, Hosted alone is a higher-risk option: tail latency can vary due to multi-tenant contention and autoscale cold-starts.

2) Would we recommend Dedicated?
   - Yes — Dedicated/Reserved capacity is the recommended path to hit consistent p95 <= 50ms across spikes. A reserved GPU pool with pinned capacity provides predictable kernel placement, steady KV cache residency, and isolation from noisy neighbors.

3) Mitigations if you want to start on Hosted:
   - Warmup routes + prefix/KV caching for common prompts (you mentioned many similar prompts). That will reduce per-token work for repeated calls.
   - Priority routing: we can pin a small dedicated slice (burst pool) to absorb short spikes with lower tail impact.
   - Canary the critical endpoints on Dedicated while keeping lower-priority traffic on Hosted.

Next steps I propose:
- Run a short benchmark (we'll replay your sample CSV) for both Hosted (with caching enabled) and Dedicated (simulated reserved capacity) to collect p95/p99 under an identical load pattern.
- If Dedicated looks required, we'll size a 2–4 GPU reserved pool for an initial pilot with autoscale thresholds tuned to your 220 QPS bursts.
- I'll send a pilot checklist and suggested timeline; procurement can loop in on sizing and term options.

Attached: pilot-checklist.pdf — includes what we'll need from your side (API keys, representative prompts, traffic replay window). If that plan sounds good I can schedule the benchmark next week.

Short timeline options: benchmark 10/18–10/20, pilot kickoff 10/25 (if Dedicated).

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0124

Jordan — thanks, that aligns with what we suspected. A few clarifying points from engineering & procurement:

- Engineering confirms that 64-token responses and the caching pattern make p95 achievable if the KV cache hit rate is >70%. We'll try to extract a sample cache-hit histogram for you by Monday.
- Procurement asked about minimum commitment for Dedicated and whether we can run an initial 2-week pilot with a credit arrangement before committing to 3/6/12 month reserved capacity. They'd like to avoid long-term commits before verifying tail behavior.

If Redwood can run the benchmark next week (10/18–10/20) and support a short pilot window with a prepaid credit or refundable trial, that would be ideal. Also, what telemetry will you provide from the benchmark? We need token-level latency histograms, p50/p95/p99, and CPU/GPU utilization curves.

Happy to approve the benchmark window — let me know what you need to proceed.

—Alex
